# Siren core — Class Diagram support

## Problem

`@siren/core` renders two diagram kinds: `flowchart` and `sequenceDiagram`. Class diagrams are
the next most commonly authored Mermaid diagram and the next Layer-1 item on
`.dev/mermaid-diagram-roadmap.md`. Unlike sequence diagrams — which needed a hand-rolled
lane/row layout because they are not a graph — a class diagram *is* a directed graph of boxes
and relationships: structurally the same problem `layoutGraph.ts` already solves with dagre for
flowcharts. That makes this board as much a chance to pay down a coming duplication (state, ER,
requirement and C4 diagrams are all graph-shaped too) as to add a diagram kind.

## Outcome

A developer can write a `classDiagram` document — classes with typed, visibility-marked members;
all eight Mermaid relationship types with labels and multiplicity; annotations; generics;
namespaces; notes; `direction`; interaction (`click`) and per-element styling (`style`,
`classDef`, `cssClass`) — pass it to the existing `render(source, container)` entry point, and
see a correctly laid-out, correctly themed SVG class diagram mounted into the DOM. A `timeline:`
block animates classes and relationships exactly as it does flowchart nodes and edges, so a
class diagram is a first-class Siren document rather than a static picture. `%%` comment lines
work in every diagram kind. Flowchart and sequence rendering are unchanged.

## Scope

- `classDiagram` header (and Mermaid's `classDiagram-v2` alias).
- **Class definitions**: `class Animal`, the block form `class Animal { ... }`, the inline member
  form `Animal : +int age`, and **implicit creation from a relationship** (`Animal <|-- Duck`
  declares both) — matching both Mermaid's canonical examples and this repo's own flowchart
  behavior, where `A --> B` creates both nodes.
- **Members**: attributes and methods; visibility markers `+` public, `-` private, `#` protected,
  `~` package; classifiers `*` abstract and `$` static; return types (`+isMammal() bool`);
  generics (`class Square~Shape~`, `List~int~`).
- **Relationships**, all eight: `<|--` inheritance, `*--` composition, `o--` aggregation, `-->`
  association, `--` solid link, `..>` dependency, `..|>` realization, `..` dashed link — each
  with an optional `: label` and optional multiplicity on either end (`Customer "1" --> "*" Ticket`).
- **Annotations**: `<<interface>>`, `<<abstract>>`, `<<enumeration>>`, `<<Service>>`, and any
  other author-chosen text, in the block form or standalone.
- **Namespaces**: `namespace Name { class A ... }`, rendered as a frame enclosing its members.
- **Notes**: `note "text"` and `note for ClassName "text"`.
- **`direction TB | BT | LR | RL`**.
- **Interaction**: `click ClassName href "url"` renders the class as a link;
  `click ClassName call fn()` and `callback ClassName "fn"` are delivered to a caller-supplied
  `render(source, container, { onClick })` handler.
- **Styling**: `style ClassName fill:#fdd,stroke:#c00`, `classDef name ...` + `cssClass "A,B" name`
  — emitted as inline `style` attributes on the target elements, so an author's local emphasis
  overrides the theme's global default without competing with it.
- **`%%` comment lines** — stripped in the shared `parseSiren` dispatcher, so flowchart, sequence
  and class documents all gain them at once. A pre-existing gap in every kind.
- **Animation**: a `timeline:` block referencing class ids and relationship ids, driving the
  existing `enter`/`exit`/`highlight`/`unhighlight` vocabulary through the existing
  `createAnimationController`.
- **Theme**: `theme/default.css` rules for every class the new renderer emits, enforced by
  extending the existing coverage test in `theme/default.test.ts`.
- **Shared layout core**: `layoutDirectedGraph`, extracted from `layoutGraph`, owning all dagre
  wiring (including compound/cluster graphs and edge-label space) behind our own interface;
  `layoutGraph` becomes a thin flowchart adapter over it with identical behavior.

## Non-goals

- Widening the **flowchart** header's direction support (still `TD|LR` only) — `direction` is a
  class-diagram statement here, not a cross-kind change.
- Changing sequence diagrams in any way, including their still-deferred activation bars, notes,
  and animation integration.
- Mermaid's exact pixel-level note placement or its cluster-margin heuristics — we place notes
  and namespace frames sensibly, not identically.
- `classDef` inheritance/cascade semantics beyond "apply these declarations to these elements";
  no specificity model.
- Styling directives for flowchart or sequence documents — this board adds them to the class
  parser only.
- Replacing `@dagrejs/dagre`. The extraction makes it *swappable* (ADR-0001's stated intent); it
  does not swap it.

## Domain decisions

- **Class**: one box in a class diagram, created by a `class` statement or implicitly by being
  named in a relationship. Its id is the declared name; a second declaration of the same name
  merges members rather than erroring (Mermaid's behavior, and consistent with flowchart's
  first-label-wins node merging).
- **Member**: one attribute or method line inside a class, carrying an optional visibility marker,
  an optional classifier, a name, an optional type, and — for methods — a parameter list and an
  optional return type. Attributes and methods render in two separate compartments, in
  declaration order within each.
- **Relationship**: a directed edge between two classes, carrying one of the eight Mermaid types,
  an optional label, and optional multiplicity strings at each end. Its id follows the flowchart
  edge convention exactly: `${fromId}-${toId}`, then `#2` for a repeat pair.
- **Relationship type**: modeled as two axes, like sequence's arrows — a `line` (`solid` |
  `dashed`) and an `endpoint` marker at the from-end and/or to-end (`none` | `triangle` (`<|`) |
  `diamondFilled` (`*`) | `diamondHollow` (`o`) | `arrow` (`>`)). The eight Mermaid forms are
  compositions of these; the renderer switches on two small enums, not eight opaque names.
- **Namespace**: a named group of classes drawn as an enclosing frame. Implemented as a dagre
  compound-graph cluster — verified feasible against the installed `@dagrejs/dagre` 3.1.1, which
  returns a cluster bounding box from `setParent`.
- **Note**: a free-standing annotation box, optionally attached to one class. A note is laid out
  as an ordinary node in the graph — attached notes joined to their class by an edge that renders
  as a connector, free notes with no edge. Because it is a real node, the layout engine itself
  guarantees a note never overlaps a class box; the cost is that a note occupies a rank and
  therefore pushes the classes around it. (Corrected after round 3: this said "an unranked node
  joined by an invisible edge", which was aspirational — nothing implemented it and the reviewer
  found the built behavior differs. Structural non-overlap is worth the nudge; revisit only if a
  real diagram lays out badly because of it.)
- **Interaction target**: a class the author made clickable. `href` URLs are restricted to an
  allowlist of `http`, `https` and `mailto`; a `javascript:` or `data:` URL is dropped with an
  error diagnostic rather than rendered. `style` declaration values reject `url(` and
  `expression(`. This extends the existing hard invariant (label text always via `textContent`,
  never `innerHTML`) to the two new author-controlled sinks this board introduces.
- **Author style**: a `style`/`classDef`/`cssClass` declaration, emitted as an inline `style`
  attribute on the target element. The theme's `--siren-*` tokens remain the global default for
  every diagram; an author style is a local override within one document. The two do not compete
  — see the ADR this board records.
- **SVG conventions** (frozen now so the pipeline-stage tickets can be built independently):
  - `<g class="siren-class" data-siren-id="{id}">` — a `<rect class="siren-class-frame">`, a
    `<text class="siren-class-name">`, an optional `<text class="siren-class-annotation">`, a
    `<line class="siren-class-divider">` above each non-empty compartment, and one
    `<text class="siren-member">` per attribute/method line.
  - `<g class="siren-relationship" data-siren-id="{id}" data-siren-relationship="{type}">`
    containing a `<path class="siren-relationship-line">` (marker-start/marker-end per endpoint,
    `stroke-dasharray` for `dashed`), an optional `<text class="siren-relationship-label">`, and
    up to two `<text class="siren-multiplicity">`.
  - `data-siren-relationship` carries the canonical Mermaid name for the composed
    `{ line, fromEnd, toEnd }`: `inheritance`, `composition`, `aggregation`, `association`,
    `link`, `dependency`, `realization`, `dashedLink`. A mirrored spelling reports the same name
    as its counterpart. A combination Mermaid has no name for falls back to a composed
    `{line}-{fromEnd}-{toEnd}` descriptor. (Frozen after round 2, which invented this vocabulary
    because the spec had not pinned it — recorded here before the closing ticket asserts on it.)
  - Endpoint markers are four `<marker>` defs. The two diamonds share one path shape and are
    told apart only by a fill class: `siren-arrow-fill` (composition) versus `siren-arrow-hollow`
    (aggregation), the latter filled with the surface color rather than left transparent so the
    relationship line does not show through it. `siren-arrow-hollow` is therefore a **load-bearing
    class, not decoration** — without a theme rule for it, composition and aggregation are
    indistinguishable on screen. Same for the hollow triangle shared by inheritance and
    realization.
  - `<g class="siren-namespace" data-siren-id="{id}">` — a `<rect class="siren-namespace-frame">`
    plus a `<text class="siren-namespace-label">`, rendered before (behind) its member classes.
  - `<g class="siren-note" data-siren-id="{id}">` — a `<rect class="siren-note-frame">` plus one
    `<text class="siren-note-text">`; an attached note also emits a
    `<path class="siren-note-link">`.
  - A clickable class is wrapped in `<a class="siren-link">` when it has an `href`, and carries
    `data-siren-click="{target}"` when it has a callback.
  - All text set via `textContent`, never `innerHTML` — unchanged hard invariant.
  - Animation classes (`siren-pending`, `siren-enter-*`, …) apply to `.siren-class`,
    `.siren-relationship`, `.siren-namespace` and `.siren-note` elements exactly as they do to
    flowchart nodes and edges. (Widened after ticket 15: the model assigns namespaces and notes
    their own ids and a `timeline:` block can address them, and an addressable element that
    cannot start hidden makes `enter` meaningless for it.)

## Design contract

### `packages/core/src/layout/layoutDirectedGraph.ts` (new — the shared core)

- Responsibilities: own every interaction with `@dagrejs/dagre` — graph construction, `rankdir`,
  compound/cluster parentage, edge-label space reservation, running the layout, and converting
  dagre's center-based node coordinates to top-left. Takes sizes it is given; returns coordinates.
- Non-responsibilities: measures no text, knows no diagram kind, no labels' content, no shapes,
  no timelines. It never sees a `GraphModel` or a `ClassModel`.
- Interface: `layoutDirectedGraph(input: DirectedGraphLayoutInput): DirectedGraphLayoutResult`,
  where the input carries `rankdir`, nodes (`id`, `width`, `height`, optional `parentId`, optional
  `isCluster`), and edges (`id`, `from`, `to`, optional label `width`/`height`); the result carries
  per-node boxes (top-left `x`/`y` plus `width`/`height`), per-edge `points` and optional label
  anchor, and the graph's overall `width`/`height`. Pure and deterministic.
- Seam: the function itself. Its types live in this module, not `contracts.ts` — they are the
  interface between two layout modules, not a cross-pipeline contract, and keeping them here is
  what lets this ticket run in parallel with the contracts freeze.
- Dependencies: `@dagrejs/dagre` (real, in tests too — pure and deterministic, as ADR-0001 notes).

### Parser (`packages/core/src/parser/`)

- Responsibilities: `parseSiren` gains a third header branch (`classDiagram`, `classDiagram-v2`)
  and, before dispatching, strips `%%` comment lines for **every** kind.
  `parseClassDiagram(source): ParseResult` recognizes every statement in Scope above and reports
  syntax problems as diagnostics without throwing.
- Non-responsibilities: does not merge duplicate class declarations, assign ids, or validate URLs
  and style values — all the model's job. It *does* declare a class named only by a relationship,
  exactly as `parseFlowchart` declares a node named only by an edge; declaring is the parser's job,
  reconciling is the model's. (Corrected after round 1's review: the original wording listed
  implicit declaration as a model responsibility, which contradicted both ticket 01's own worked
  example and the flowchart precedent the parser follows.)
- Interface: `parseSiren(source: string): ParseResult` (unchanged signature);
  `parseClassDiagram(source: string): ParseResult` (new, independently testable).
- Seam: both functions — string in, data out.
- Dependencies: none.

### Graph model (`packages/core/src/graph-model/`)

- Responsibilities: `buildGraphModel` gains a third dispatch branch.
  `buildClassModel(document: ClassDocument): { model: ClassModel | null; diagnostics: Diagnostic[] }`
  creates classes implicitly from relationships, merges duplicate declarations, assigns
  relationship ids, resolves namespace membership and note attachment, validates interaction URLs
  against the allowlist and style values against the rejected-function list, and resolves the
  `timeline:` block against class and relationship ids.
- Non-responsibilities: no coordinates, no rendering.
- Interface: `buildGraphModel(document: SirenDocument): GraphModelResult` (unchanged signature,
  gains a `classModel` field alongside `graph`/`model`);
  `buildClassModel(document: ClassDocument): ClassModelResult` (new).
- Seam: `buildClassModel` itself, testable with hand-built `ClassDocument` fixtures.
- Dependencies: none.

### Layout (`packages/core/src/layout/layoutClassDiagram.ts`, new)

- Responsibilities: measure every class box (name, annotation, and each member line — box width is
  the widest line, height the sum plus dividers and padding), measure relationship labels and
  multiplicity, map namespaces to clusters and notes to nodes, call `layoutDirectedGraph`, and
  return a `PositionedClassDiagram` carrying each class's compartment boundaries, each
  relationship's path and label anchors, each namespace's frame, and each note's box.
- Non-responsibilities: no dagre (that is the shared core's), no SVG, no styling.
- Interface: `layoutClassDiagram(model: ClassModel, options: LayoutOptions): PositionedClassDiagram`.
  Reuses the existing `LayoutOptions`/`TextMeasurer` seam unchanged.
- Seam: the `TextMeasurer` injection point — fake in tests, real in the browser.
- Dependencies: `layoutDirectedGraph` (in-process, real in tests).

### Renderer (`packages/core/src/renderer/renderClassDiagramToSVG.ts`, new)

- Responsibilities: build the SVG tree per the frozen conventions above — class boxes with
  compartments, all eight relationship line/marker combinations, labels and multiplicity,
  namespace frames, notes, author inline styles, links and click hooks, and the initial
  `siren-pending` class for animated elements.
- Non-responsibilities: no layout, no event listeners (the click *hook* is an attribute; `index.ts`
  attaches the listener), no theme colors (those live in `default.css`).
- Interface: `renderClassDiagramToSVG(diagram: PositionedClassDiagram): SVGSVGElement`.
- Seam: the DOM — jsdom in tests, browser in the demo.
- Dependencies: DOM only.

### Public API (`packages/core/src/index.ts`)

- Responsibilities: `render()` gains a third `kind` branch running
  `buildClassModel → layoutClassDiagram → renderClassDiagramToSVG → createAnimationController`,
  and a new `RenderOptions.onClick?: (target: { id: string; action: string }) => void` that it
  attaches to elements carrying `data-siren-click`.
- Non-responsibilities: no diagram-type detection beyond what `parseSiren` does.
- Interface: `render(source, container, options?): SirenRenderResult` — signature unchanged;
  `RenderOptions` gains one optional field.
- Seam: the primary end-to-end integration seam.
- Dependencies: composes the modules above.

### Theme (`packages/core/src/theme/`)

- Responsibilities: `default.css` gains rules for every class the class renderer emits;
  `default.test.ts` gains a class-diagram coverage block reusing its existing generic helpers
  (`renderThemedSVG`, `emittedSirenClasses`) — only a new every-feature source constant is needed.
- Non-responsibilities: does not restyle flowchart or sequence rules.
- Interface: the stylesheet itself, per ADR-0004.
- Seam: the coverage test, which fails when the renderer emits a class the theme does not select.
- Dependencies: DOM/jsdom cascade.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `render()` on `flowchart` and `sequenceDiagram` documents behaves exactly as before — the
      existing 179 tests pass unmodified.
- [ ] `%%` comment lines are ignored in all three diagram kinds, including at the end of a line
      of real syntax, and a document that is only comments produces a diagnostic rather than a
      crash.
- [ ] `render()` on a `classDiagram` with `Animal <|-- Duck` and no `class` statement mounts an
      SVG with two `<g class="siren-class">` and one `<g class="siren-relationship">`.
- [ ] A class declared in block form with attributes and methods renders one compartment per
      populated group, separated by `<line class="siren-class-divider">`, with visibility markers,
      classifiers, types and return types preserved verbatim in the member text.
- [ ] Each of the eight relationship types renders its own line style and endpoint markers, all
      backed by distinct `<marker>` defs; labels and both multiplicity strings render when given.
- [ ] `<<interface>>` renders a `<text class="siren-class-annotation">`; generics render as part
      of the class name text.
- [ ] A `namespace` renders one `<g class="siren-namespace">` frame enclosing every member class's
      box, painted behind them.
- [ ] `note for X "..."` renders a note box plus a connector to X's box; `note "..."` renders a box
      with no connector.
- [ ] `direction LR` changes the layout's rank direction versus the same document without it.
- [ ] `click X href "https://example.com"` wraps X in `<a class="siren-link">`; a `javascript:` URL
      is dropped with an error diagnostic and no `<a>` is emitted.
- [ ] `click X call fn()` emits `data-siren-click`, and `render(..., { onClick })` receives the
      target when that element is clicked.
- [ ] `style X fill:#fdd` puts those declarations in X's inline `style` attribute; a value
      containing `url(` is dropped with an error diagnostic.
- [ ] A `timeline:` block referencing a class id and a relationship id marks them `siren-pending`
      and reveals them through `controller.next()`, exactly as for a flowchart.
- [ ] `theme/default.css` has a rule selecting every `siren-*` class the class renderer emits, and
      every drawn element resolves a stroke or a fill — enforced by `theme/default.test.ts`.
- [ ] `demos/class-diagram.html`, built against the real Vite bundle, visibly renders a class
      diagram exercising every feature in scope, in both light and dark theme.

## Test strategy

- `layoutDirectedGraph` — unit, pure function, real dagre, hand-built size inputs.
- `parseClassDiagram` / `parseSiren` dispatch and comment stripping — unit, pure functions.
- `buildClassModel` — unit, pure function, hand-built `ClassDocument` fixtures.
- `layoutClassDiagram` — unit, pure function, fake deterministic `TextMeasurer`.
- `renderClassDiagramToSVG` — component test under jsdom, hand-built `PositionedClassDiagram`
  fixtures.
- `render()` — integration under jsdom for every acceptance criterion above except the last.
- Theme — the existing cascade-based coverage tests, extended with a class-diagram source.
- The demo page is verified by rasterizing the rendered SVG with the stylesheet applied and
  looking at the image; automated browser e2e remains out of scope, as on previous boards.

## Verification

- Focused: `pnpm --filter @siren/core exec vitest run <file>`
  (note: `pnpm --filter @siren/core test -- <file>` does **not** filter in this repo — it runs
  the whole suite)
- Suite: `pnpm --filter @siren/core test`
- Static: `pnpm --filter @siren/core exec tsc --noEmit`

## Baseline

Measured 2026-09-04 on `main` at `30718e8` (the sequence-diagram merge): `pnpm --filter
@siren/core test` — 11 test files, 179 tests, all passing. `pnpm --filter @siren/core exec tsc
--noEmit` — 0 errors. Clean baseline; any failure surfacing during this board is new.

## Risks and deferred questions

- **The shared-core extraction touches shipped flowchart code.** `layoutGraph` is load-bearing for
  every flowchart and has 65 tests plus the whole animation suite behind it. The extraction ticket
  must leave those tests untouched and passing — if it needs to change one, that is a signal the
  behavior moved, not that the test was wrong.
- **Interaction and styling are new sinks for untrusted author input.** The board treats the URL
  allowlist and the style-value rejection list as hard requirements with their own acceptance
  criteria, but a fuller review (attribute-injection edge cases beyond these two sinks) is
  deferred, exactly as the first slice deferred it for label text.
- **This board records an ADR**: author-level styling (`style`/`classDef`/`cssClass`) sits
  alongside ADR-0004's token-based theme. The decision — global theme as default, author
  directives as local inline override — is load-bearing, surprising without context, and had a
  real alternative (generating a `<style>` block with generated class names). It gets written up
  when the styling ticket lands.
- **Ticket count.** Near-complete Mermaid class-diagram parity plus a refactor of shipped layout
  code plus a cross-cutting comment fix plus animation is a large board — 17 tickets in four
  waves. Nothing here is speculative: every item was confirmed in the planning interview.
- **`direction` asymmetry.** Class diagrams will accept `TB|BT|LR|RL` while flowcharts still only
  accept `TD|LR`. That inconsistency is deliberate for this board and worth its own ticket later.
